subject: MSA / Security Exhibit: redlines, inspection scope, and evidence rotation
messages:
From: Ryan Chen <ryan.chen@helixlabs.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, contracts@redwood.ai
Cc: Helix Labs Legal <contracts@helixlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Security Exhibit - redlines + evidence cadence questions

Laura / Redwood team,

Thanks for sending the MSA and security exhibit. Attached are the redlines Helix Legal compiled (Helix_redlines_MSASecurityExhibit_v1.docx). A few items we want to call out and get clarity on: 

- Pen test/inspection notice: the current draft says "reasonable notice" — can we get a fixed minimum notice window for scheduling (30/45 days)? We need time to coordinate our security team.
- Scope of inspection: can you confirm whether inspections include production access, or are they limited to replicas/staging? For regulated data we need explicit limitations.
- SOC 2 evidence: will Redwood provide copy of the most recent SOC 2 report? What is your turnaround to attest to controls on request?
- Evidence cadence: we prefer a scheduled annual evidence package rather than ad-hoc requests; if ad-hoc is needed, define emergency criteria.

Can we get written responses to the above and a short joint call next week to walk through? Ryan and Michael are on copies — they can join the call.

Thanks,
Ryan Chen
Head of Security Operations
Helix Labs

Attachments: Helix_redlines_MSASecurityExhibit_v1.docx (file stub)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Chen <ryan.chen@helixlabs.com>, Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@helixlabs.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Security Exhibit - redlines + evidence cadence questions

Ryan — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Appreciate the level of detail; we want to make this low-friction. High-level responses below and next steps at the bottom. Attaching a marked-up security exhibit (Redwood_Security_Exhibit_response_v2.pdf) with inline language we think will close most items.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Notice window for pen test/inspection: Redwood proposes a 45-calendar-day standard notice for planned inspections. We can accommodate 30 days for low-impact scans but need 45 for full-scope engagements.
- Scope: our standard position is inspections are scoped to customer-specific tenant data and non-production replicas unless mutually agreed. Production access for manual inspection is available only under a narrow, pre-approved exception with additional controls (read-only session, scoped accounts, and timeboxed access).
- SOC 2 evidence: we provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted where necessary) on request via our secure portal. Typical turnaround to grant access is 3 business days to validate request and share the report; if you need a specific assertion letter, allow 10 business days for legal/KYC review.
- Evidence cadence: we are happy to commit to an annual packaged evidence delivery (SOC 2 + supporting artifacts) and an agreed ad-hoc process for emergency investigations (incident-based, with documented triggers in the exhibit).

Suggested contract language highlights in the attached:
- Define "Bounded Inspection" section that limits frequency to annual full-scope and a maximum of two targeted follow-ups per 12 months unless critical incident.
- Spell out notice windows (30/45 days) and emergency escalation path.
- Add explicit language about redaction and non-disclosure of platform-level metrics and other third-party tenant data.

Next steps: 
1) Internal: Priyom/legal to confirm any items that require alternate wording (Priyom — see inline comments on pages 3–4).
2) Internal: Karthik/security to confirm technical controls we can commit to for scoped production access (Karthik — please confirm RDP/session tooling and audit logs).
3) External: Proposed joint call Friday 2029-09-13 at 11:00 AM PT to review redlines and finalize language (Ryan / Michael — does that work?).

If call works we can run a 30–45 minute session: legal + security + technical. I’ll follow up with a calendar invite and a DocuSign pre-filled MSA if we align.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA / Security Exhibit - legal redline suggestions (internal)

Laura / team — quick legal view on the proposed responses. I pulled the attached suggested redline set and highlighted a few problem areas. Summary below; see inline comments in the Drive link.

Key recommendations:
- Replace broad "audit rights" phrasing with "assurance review rights" and define a narrow scope: 
  - Customer may request review of evidence related to their tenant and controls affecting their data only.
  - Platform-level artifacts (multi-tenant telemetry, third-party vendor logs, internal dev logs) are out of scope.
- Pen test language: we should be explicit that Redwood will support customer-procured pen tests against scoped endpoints and offer a parallel option where Redwood can run a supervised test. For customer-run tests require a mutually-agreed statement of work and 45-day scheduling minimum.
- Evidence release SLAs: commit to 3 business days to validate requests and 10 business days to provide full artifact sets where permissible.
- Emergency access exceptions: define "critical incident" narrowly (confirmed data-exfiltration, active EV, regulator subpoena) and require joint governance call before additional intrusive access.

Process note: If Helix accepts the narrowed scope and the SLA language, we can offer a one-time concession: a secondary evidence package in year one to support onboarding (customer request within first 90 days). After that, cadence reverts to annual unless incident.

Doc links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A_redwood_internal/msas/helix (internal)
Redline files: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_response_v2.pdf (already shared in thread)

I’ll be on the call Friday to walk legal redlines.

—Priyom
Senior Corporate Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Chen <ryan.chen@helixlabs.com>, Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@helixlabs.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: MSA Security Exhibit — agreed approach and next steps

Ryan / Michael — following internal review we’re aligned on the approach. Quick summary and action items before Friday: 

What we will accept/commit to:
- 45-day notice for full-scope pen tests; 30 days for low-impact scans.
- Inspections limited to customer tenant artifacts and non-prod replicas by default; production access requires pre-approval and additional controls.
- SOC 2 Type II available via secure portal; 3 business day validation + 10 business day artifact turnaround for requests.
- Annual evidence package as standard cadence + one onboarding package in year one (if requested within 90 days).
- Emergency/incident process spelled out in exhibit with narrow triggers and governance steps.

Action items / next steps:
1) I will send an updated redline PDF (attached previously) to Helix legal and request confirmation on the two outstanding items: (a) whether they want production access language at all and (b) accept the 45-day notice.
2) Priyom will include final clause text for the "assurance review" replacement and upload the version we want to track in DocuSign.
3) Karthik will confirm operational steps (session tooling + audit log retention) and post to the Drive folder by EOD Thursday.
4) Proposed call: Fri 2029-09-13 11:00 AM PT — calendar invite to follow.

If you can confirm the call slot, we’ll finalize language and run the MSA through DocuSign the same day if there are no further material edits.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the constructive collaboration.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference
